title: An MI300X Over MCP: What the Matrix Cores Execute, and What They Don't
why_read: A hands-on, rigorously measured benchmarking report of AMD's MI300X GPU numeric formats via a custom MCP tool is a substantive piece for anyone doing ML infrastructure work on AMD hardware.
analysis: This post describes building a set of MCP (Model Context Protocol) tools to remotely manage and benchmark a single AMD Instinct MI300X GPU, focusing on measuring which numeric formats (fp8, int8, fp4) the hardware actually supports and how they perform relative to each other. The author found fp8 e4m3fnuz runs 1.77x faster than bf16, int8 runs slower at 0.69x despite AMD rating it the same as fp8, and fp4 isn't supported at all on this chip, correcting some readings that didn't match AMD's published specs. This kind of first-hand, verified hardware benchmarking is valuable because it catches discrepancies between vendor marketing numbers and actual measured behavior, which matters a lot for ML engineers choosing numeric precision for training or inference. The MCP tooling angle is also a practical example of using LLM-agent-style tool interfaces for infrastructure management tasks.
